rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 37: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work. | 5: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut both lines; the tracker read carries its own substance and neither sentence tells the student what to do next.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Author-we ban, first-person-plural extension.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 49: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut. Substituting 'the training authors' for 'we' makes the sentence read as a manifesto beside a ticket-writing beat; the editorial-stance flourish goes with the pronoun.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing, run the truth test before reaching for section 12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 24: Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: No true reading exists (an agent editing a test breaks it, and this training's own fix-tests-first beat has the agent working on tests). Cut rather than hedge.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 55: ## Anything can be reverse-engineered | section carries only two bullets (57, 58), no boundary paragraph
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Restore one Boris-direct boundary bullet naming what limits the read, e.g. extraction quality tracks the quality of the artifact sampled. The file's own stance block at L134 asserts the boundary sits in a third bullet that is not present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: M1 exercise; subagent and compaction boundary are unearned at this arc position and this is operational copy, where earning elsewhere does not carry. Cut the line.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pronoun/metaphor-referent check fires on ANY closer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: Wire this through the subagent context window
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: 'this' has no antecedent; the preceding line is the What you build widget. Cold read cannot resolve what is being wired.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consultancy register, not the AE101 quintet; 'unlocks' plus 'transformational value' is the growth-hack shape the slang test rejects, and it sells rather than teaches on line 5 of a 20-minute exercise.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words, grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: derive-body-view greps over lines 1-65: em_dash body_hits 0 CLEAN, banned_words body_hits 0 CLEAN, ritual_ceremony 0 CLEAN, leverage_verb 0 CLEAN, each with planted_proof true. Closest call is line 5 'unlocks transformational value', consultancy register but not on the list; filed under section 4 and section 13 instead.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest line is 30: 'No ticket of your own to read? Any other real ticket from your tracker works.' That is a fallback with a mechanism, not a reassurance about the reader's standing, and it carries the follow-on constraint in the next clause. No 'no penalty' / 'fine way to' / 'you are not on the hook' shapes in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 39: 'Push back on the five.' The five rules are produced by the agent at runtime and are not a visible list on the page, so the numeral is the memory handle the carve-out protects. 62: 'Two things came out of one ticket' is section 16 move 1 (count + noun), prescribed rather than banned.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The What happened block is OPTIONAL; standard shape when included is three moves.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 62-64 runs count+noun ('Two things'), one qualifier ('the conventions your team has been encoding in its fields all along'), and past tense throughout ('came out', 'closed'). Move 3 is where line 64 goes wrong, but as a cartography fault, filed under check_student_facing section 33.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A sentence saying how you'd know points at the outcome, not the nearest artifact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 53: 'Does it sound like the comments already on the ticket?' points at an external artifact the student did not generate, so the observation can come back negative. Not self-witnessing.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching; every instruction line names an actor AND a mechanism, and must be executable.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Third axis: the student cannot perform this and could not tell whether they had. No actor, no mechanism, no observable result. Cut, or move the real move into a prompt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: the subagent context window ... the compaction boundary
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: The maintainer accept-note at L72 covers 'connector' only. 'Compaction boundary' is house/platform vocabulary, not the industry-standard tier the 2026-08-18 carve-out exempts, and nothing in this file or an upstream M1 beat lands it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself; subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 64: The next exercise sweeps this whole session.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Predicate leak named in the 2026-08-23 amendment: a clause promising what a later beat will do is cartography whatever its subject. The preceding sentence ('The field rules stay in the scrollback.') joins cleanly to the section above without it. Not in an exempt signposting section.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation. | 24: Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Neither changes what the student understands, decides, does or notices next; line 24 also sits between a ticket-reading prompt and a conventions section it has no relation to. Run NVA before the truth test on line 24.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No tier-pegging and no deficiency assertion in the body. The identity-criterion trap is absent; line 13 'the agent can reverse-engineer your team's rules' names a capability of the agent, not a bar the student must clear.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Split is held: 57 'reverse-engineered with an LLM' (capability/thinking), 58 'Ask the agent to study' (acting), 33/45/53 'Ask Claude to ...' (addressee). Body agent-count and Claude-count are balanced, no assistant-shaped skew.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: em_dash grep over body region lines 1-65: body_hits 0, status CLEAN, planted_proof true.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.

The depth-counted '../' prefix is path form, governed by curriculum/module-shape.md and out of this rule's scope per the 2026-08-13 clarification; noted for the technical class.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Four of five headers lead with a verb (Read / Read / Write / Double-check). '## Anything can be reverse-engineered' is declarative, but its section is the closing frame rather than a doing beat, and its defect is the missing boundary bullet filed under check_writing section 12.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Expanded view (scripts/expand-md.js output at curriculum/evals/body-views/shared--file--writing-5judge.expanded.md) shows no bracket placeholders in any of the three fences. Prompt 1 ends on the open-hook 'Ticket:' with the student input genuinely required, matching fix (d).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 20 'Drop the ticket link after the colon.' is exactly the 2a sub-case shape for a fence ending in a dangling colon. 33 and 45 are 14 and 13 words, both command-verb led. 45 is the closest call, mirroring three of prompt 3's four clauses, but the fence carries four moves and cannot be held in one glance.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt 3 closes 'Tell me what you wrote.' after a side-effecting ticket update, which is the post-action report this rule asks for; a tracker comment is reversible so the irreversible-action carve-out does not apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Three sell-shaped lines land inside a teaching beat whose AE101 M1 mood is earned trust. Marketing register in the first five lines is the signature wrong-edit for this position; the mood recovers on cutting them.

findings.quote: Unlike vendor tooling that locks your team in, this approach keeps you in control of the work.
findings.harm: The rule prevents a teaching beat from reading as a defence of the training against competitors; the student stops learning and starts being sold to, and engineers who read citations and decide for themselves register the defensiveness. Present here in the hard sub-rule's exact shape: 'Unlike ...' plus 'vendor', which the rule says to treat as suspect every time.
findings.fix: Cut the sentence. Nothing downstream depends on it.

findings.quote: This capability unlocks transformational value across your entire delivery organisation.
findings.harm: Same harm, marketing-deck register imported into the body. It arrives before the student has done anything, so the first full sentence of the exercise is a value claim rather than a move.
findings.fix: Cut. Line 7's 'What you do' already tells the student what the beat is.

findings.quote: We believe the loop matters more than the model, and we built this training around that.
findings.harm: Author-we hands the body to the training-as-organisation. Substituting 'the training authors' for 'we' makes the sentence read as a manifesto, and the rule's editorial-flourish clause fires on the second half, which is pure positioning.
findings.fix: Cut both halves. Recasting to 'The loop matters more than the model' would keep a claim this exercise never earns.

findings.quote: Every test you write is a test the agent can never break.
findings.harm: The rule prevents a false superlative shipping as a memorable line. 'never' is asserted about how the world works, and the counterexample is one file over: this training has the agent working on tests, where it can and does change them. A professional audience finds the counterexample faster than the author does.
findings.fix: Cut. Hedging to 'usually never' makes it worse; the surrounding beat is about ticket conventions and does not need a test aphorism.

findings.quote: Wire this through the subagent context window before you hit the compaction boundary.
findings.harm: Three harms in one line. Jargon planted too early pre-spoils a later module's clean teach and lifts vocabulary the M1 student would not use back to themselves. The line is also unexecutable, so the student cannot do it or tell whether they had. And 'this' has no antecedent, so a cold read cannot resolve what is being wired.
findings.fix: Cut the line. It sits between the What you build and The point widgets and nothing refers back to it.

findings.harm: The rule keeps a sharp slogan sharp by putting its boundary one paragraph downstream. Here the slogan lands and no boundary follows: the section carries two bullets (57, 58), both expansion, none limiting. The file's own stance block asserts at L134 that the boundary 'lives in the third bullet' and instructs judges to read it before flagging, so the standing accept-note's own precondition is unmet.
findings.fix: Restore one Boris-direct boundary bullet after 57 naming what limits the read (extraction quality tracks the quality of the artifact sampled), or correct the stance block.

findings.quote: The next exercise sweeps this whole session.
findings.harm: The rule prevents the training narrating its own shape to the student. This is the predicate leak named in the 2026-08-23 amendment: a clause promising what a later beat will do, which is a cheque that beat must cash. Deletion test passes, the preceding sentence stands alone.
findings.fix: Cut the clause; keep 'The field rules stay in the scrollback.'

todos.note: Stance block asserts the Anything-can-be-reverse-engineered boundary sits in 'the third bullet', which no longer exists. Keep-notes bind to their passage; the clause needs rewriting in the same pass as the body fix. Below the maintainer cut, so out of writing-class body scope, recorded for the maintainer.
Link text is correct; the depth-counted '../trainings/...' path prefix is forbidden by curriculum/module-shape.md, not by this rule. For the technical class to confirm.
Lead-in mirrors three of prompt 3's four clauses. Passes because the fence carries four moves, but if the prompt ever shortens, cut to the opening move.
